KO.rationale: KO is a world-class defensive franchise with elite margins (gross ~62%, operating ~34%, net ~30%), 40.4% ROE, and a 64-year dividend growth streak. However, the stock is fairly-to-slightly-rich valued at 27x PE (55th percentile of 365d range), with a 3.7% earnings yield below the 4.34% 10-year Treasury, offering no equity risk premium cushion. The narrow 2-quarter data window limits confident trend extrapolation, and the Q1 2025 OCF deficit of -$5.20B raises cash-conversion questions (though management's 2026 OCF guidance of ~$14.4B suggests seasonality). CSD volume declines in developed markets are structural, and 76% ex-US revenue creates persistent FX risk (5-6% EPS headwind in 2025). Oil at ~$99/bbl is an unquantified input-cost headwind. The Q1 2026 earnings report on April 28 (consensus EPS $0.81, +11% YoY) is a modest near-term catalyst that could confirm the steady trajectory, but is unlikely to drive a material re-rating given the already-full valuation. Net: strong business quality, fair valuation, limited upside without multiple expansion or a pullback toward the ~23x PE trough.
